No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

The course examines what sculpture, texts and living traditions reveal about wrestling and combat sports in India, and what they meant to those who practised and patronised them.

The course is run for your batch on dates you choose. Timings, pace and assessment are agreed before it begins.

What it covers

  • Wrestling and combat in sculpture and texts
  • Traditions that are still practised
  • What these sports meant to those who practised and paid for them

How the time is spent

  1. Sources 20 min

    Treat treatises, inscriptions and images as different evidence.

    You: source matrix

  2. Social setting 45 min

    Explore patronage, pedagogy and performance.

    You: historical map

  3. Continuities 25 min

    Consider living traditions without unbroken-continuity claims.

    You: interview questions

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Distinguish what treatises, inscriptions and images each reveal about wrestling and combat.
  • Explain what wrestling and combat sports meant to those who practised and patronised them.
  • Discuss living traditions of combat without assuming an unbroken continuity with the past.
